# Blinds, antes, straddles and bomb pots

*The forced bets that start the action, plus the two home-game favourites — straddles and bomb pots — and how to run them fairly.*

3 min read · Updated 2026-09-26

Without forced bets, everyone could wait for aces and nobody would ever play a hand. **Blinds** and **antes** put a few chips in the middle before the cards are dealt, so there is always something worth fighting for.

## Blinds

- The **small blind** sits directly left of the button and is usually half the big blind.
- The **big blind** sits two seats left of the button. It is also the minimum bet for the hand.
- Blinds are **live**: they count towards a call or a raise. If nobody raises, the big blind can still raise (the “option”).

A good rule for a cash-game night: one buy-in should be about **100 big blinds**. With a Poker Night buy-in size of 200 chips, play blinds of 1/2.

| Buy-in size | Blinds | Big blinds per buy-in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 100 | 1 / 1 | 100 |
| 200 | 1 / 2 | 100 |
| 500 | 2 / 5 | 100 |
| 1,000 | 5 / 10 | 100 |

> **Tip — New player joining?:** The simplest fair rule: a newcomer either posts one big blind right away or waits until the big blind reaches them. The same goes for a player who missed their blinds while away from the table.

## Antes

An **ante** is a small extra contribution before the deal. Antes make pots bigger and push people to play more hands. Cash games at home rarely use them; tournaments add them in later levels.

| Style | Who pays | Why use it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Classic ante | Every player, e.g. 10% of the big blind each | Traditional, but slow to collect and easy to forget |
| Big blind ante | Only the big blind, usually one big blind for the whole table | One payment per hand — the modern tournament standard |

## Straddles

A **straddle** is a voluntary third blind, normally **twice the big blind**, posted by the player left of the big blind **before the cards are dealt**. It works like a bigger big blind:

- Preflop action starts with the player left of the straddler.
- The straddler acts last preflop and can raise even if everyone just calls.
- The minimum raise is now based on the straddle, so the game plays one size bigger.

> **Watch out — Decide before the night starts:** Straddles quietly double the stakes. Agree whether they are allowed, who may straddle (only under the gun, or any seat), and whether a re-straddle is allowed. Tell newcomers before their first hand.

## Bomb pots

A **bomb pot** is a party hand: everyone puts in an agreed amount, **preflop betting is skipped**, and the flop comes straight away. Betting then runs as normal from the first player left of the button.

1. Agree the amount — commonly 2 to 5 big blinds each.
2. Agree when bomb pots happen — for example once per orbit, when the button reaches the host.
3. Everyone dealt in puts in the amount before the deal. Deal hole cards as usual.
4. Deal the flop and play the hand from there.

> **Note — Double-board bomb pots:** A popular variant deals two separate boards. Half the pot goes to the best hand on each board. If one player wins both, they take it all.
